design.window: Use the first accepted full-clock trigger as the ADC origin, including trials that Control would not store as qualified two-strip windows. Where present, match the first isolated input to that ADC grid.
design.scope: Fixed saved simulated injections for a positive control. Report delay from scheduled injection onsets, separately from measured rise grouping and full-clock trigger acceptance. No efficiency inference.

recorded.timing: Compare another recorded rise extent from reference plus one ADC sample through the last active sample. These inclusive sample spans describe grouped activity. A reference alone is before the first active sample.
recorded.support: Fast and slow bounds are the acquisition readout support used for ADC rail checks, including the quiet reference or trapezoid lookback and one leading correction margin. The preamplifier retains analog history beyond these finite digital sample spans.
recorded.coverage: Use each block and its own half-open qualification gaps and live endpoints. No adjacency is inferred across independently reset blocks. An incomplete support can still contain a recorded rise.
recorded.waveform: Use the all-34 signed face sums and the saved acquisition baseline. A potential second activity group needs the recorded coincidence threshold and three contiguous quiet increments visible within the sidecar. The first two ADC samples cannot yield a filtered increment. This test does not repeat persistent-step acceptance.
recorded.limitations: A single recorded or reproduced rise can contain several deposits or pulses. The diagnostic cannot exclude activity in the same group, below threshold, or outside the saved ADC interval. No simulated arrival labels enter the calculation, and no trigger or order was removed or reweighted.
recorded.representative: Use the captured two-strip window nearest another recorded rise by distance from its reference to the other rise extent. Break ties in acquisition and trigger order.

reference.clock: Each block uses its own saved lab clock in ns shared by both sources, ADC, and transport. There is no comparison across reset block boundaries.
reference.in_window: Inclusive endpoints at the first and last absolute sample in each finite support. Additional means at least two observed-in-simulation groups on that support, or one distinct from the unique timing-graph candidate. A single candidate without a unique match is uncertain. Ge groups include delayed daughters from earlier parents. Exposure-start electronics reset and qualified history rules remain in force.
reference.near: Compare inclusive 300/1000/6000 ns neighboring scheduled Ge deposit-interval gaps around a timing-graph anchor, and count parent marks and Ge group onsets in the same symmetric widths around the absolute trigger stamp. All marks include the graph anchor’s parent if present, while distinct marks exclude it.
reference.pulse: Check signed source-component current within the ADC window on all 34 contacts and separately on the four collectors. For current-bearing components, measure preamp swing on the local sample clock at the nominal analog gain. One code is an amplitude scale and supplies no ADC detectability or trigger guarantee. Old free tails are outside the native-current definition.
reference.scope: Both association and extra-source statistics use saved simulation references. The measured rearm and rise flags were frozen before comparison. No exclusions, threshold training, new transport, new drift or full ADC replay. Distinct groups can have the same decay parent.
